## Natural history notes

A small checkered-skipper characterized by dark brown to black wings marked with bold white checkered spots, a compact body, and a quick, low flight typical of skippers. In Florida, it is common in sunny open habitats such as lawns, roadsides, gardens, fields, parks, coastal areas, and disturbed sites where low-growing mallows are present. Adults feed on nectar from small flowers and often perch low on bare ground or vegetation, while the caterpillars feed on plants in the mallow family, using folded or tied leaves as shelters during development.
